cards.title: One lap decides the whole Sunday
cards.text: 22 cars, three rounds: 6 out after the first, 6 after the second, and ten left to fight for the grid that shapes everything the race can become.

cards.title: Hamilton takes it
cards.text: By 0.011s over Antonelli. Less time than a blink.

cards.title: Out before it got serious
cards.text: Bearman (P17), Ocon (P18), Perez (P19), Bottas (P20), Alonso (P21), Stroll (P22).

cards.title: So close to the top ten
cards.text: Gasly (P11), Bortoleto (P12), Hulkenberg (P13), Colapinto (P14), Sainz (P15), Albon (P16).

cards.title: 1 lap thrown in the bin
cards.text: In qualifying a deleted lap can be the difference between Q3 and going home early.

cards.title: Hamilton was quickest through the trap: 308 km/h
cards.text: Qualifying trim, wings trimmed back, nothing to lose.

cards.title: Nobody owned the whole lap
cards.text: The perfect lap of the day was never actually driven: it lives in three different cars.

cards.title: 21 yellow flag calls during the session
cards.text: A yellow in the wrong sector at the wrong moment ends somebody's lap, and sometimes their session.

cards.title: How Sunday starts
cards.text: P1 Hamilton · P2 Antonelli · P3 Verstappen · P4 Leclerc · P5 Russell · P6 Norris
bullets: Albon qualified P16 and starts P22, 6 places further back
The grid is not the qualifying order. A penalty moves a car back, whether for something on track or for a new engine, and everybody behind it moves up
